jobs.descriptionHtmlOrText:
We are seeking a deeply technical product leader to take ownership of our extensive Networking and Switches portfolio: secure console servers, managed and unmanaged PoE Ethernet switches, media converters, industrial connectivity, and serial extension solutions. This product line is central to our customers' operations across datacom, industrial, and secure government environments. We are looking for a technical authority who will drive portfolio optimization, OEM/ODM vendor management, and rigorous quality assurance, sitting at the intersection of deep hardware engineering, and product lifecycle execution. This role can be based in our Plano, TX, Lawrence, PA, or India offices to allow for direct, hands-on access to our hardware labs, though remote (US) arrangements will be considered for exceptional candidates.



What You Will Do
Technical Portfolio Strategy and Optimization: Evaluate the existing networking, converter, and console server portfolio to drive SKU rationalization, BOM optimization, and margin improvement. Identify which products to consolidate or sunset and which high-margin lines to scale.
OEM/ODM Vendor Architecture and Management: Act as the primary technical interface with our global manufacturing partners. Influence their roadmaps, negotiate technical SLAs, and drive root-cause analysis and supplier quality corrections for field failures.
Rigorous Product Engineering and QA Leadership: Own the firmware and hardware validation gate. Design and execute New Product Introduction testing, regulatory compliance verification, and automated test frameworks.
Level 3 Escalation Authority: Serve as the final technical escalation point for complex field failures. Perform hands-on debugging in the lab, translate field data into engineering requirements, and enforce corrective actions with vendors.
Engineering Impact of Compliance and Certification: Partner with the Compliance Manager, who tracks market mandates and certification requirements. You translate those mandates into hardware and firmware requirements, evaluating vendor BOMs and architectures so that component or firmware changes do not silently invalidate FIPS, TAA, UL, NERC CIP, and other relevant standards.
Lifecycle and Knowledge Execution: Manage the product lifecycle from NPI through End-of-Life. Build the technical documentation, training material, troubleshooting guides, firmware test checklists, and compatibility matrices that empower support, Product Ops, and adjacent product managers.
Cross-Portfolio Technical Collaboration: Act as the networking subject matter expert for the broader product organization, supporting Sales and Product Marketing with technical content.


Core Technical Expertise
Layer 2 and Layer 3 Networking Standards: VLANs (802.1Q), Spanning Tree Protocols (STP/RSTP/MSTP), link aggregation (LACP), QoS/CoS prioritization, IP routing (Static, OSPF), IGMP snooping, and security mechanisms like 802.1X and ACLs.
Media Conversion and Physical Layer Mechanics: Optical and copper interfaces (SFP/SFP+, RJ-45, single-mode vs. multi-mode fiber, wavelength specifications), Power over Ethernet standards, and rate-matching mechanics.
PoE System Engineering: PSE/PD classification and power budget validation across 802.3af, 802.3at, intelligent detection and backward-compatibility behavior, and downstream device power profiling.
Harsh-Environment and Industrial Specifications: Industrial hardening, wide operating temperatures, high EMC/EMI immunity, redundant power inputs, ring redundancy protocols, and DIN-rail or panel-mount deployment.
Out-of-Band Management and Connectivity Protocols: Console server architectures, secure out-of-band access, terminal emulation, serial-over-IP encapsulation, and USB extension technology.
Security, Authentication, and Compliance Implementation: How standards are physically and logically implemented in networking gear, including TPM 2.0, FIPS 140-2/3 validated cryptographic modules, TAA-compliant supply chains, and NERC CIP supporting features; AAA frameworks (TACACS+, RADIUS, Kerberos, 802.1X) and VPN technologies (OpenVPN, IPsec) as applied to secure out-of-band platforms; plus ZTP, RESTful API, and SNMP/LLDP/NTP integration.
Serial and Signal Extension Technologies: Classic serial interfaces (RS-232, RS-422, RS-485) and V.35/Coax signal conversion, along with the electrical principles of signal attenuation, impedance matching, and long-distance copper extension.
OT and Industrial Serial Practice: Modbus ASCII/RTU over RS-422/485, and serial line conditioning including bias, termination, isolation (e.g., 2-kV), and surge protection.


Who Will Succeed in This Role
You are a hands-on technical leader who is just as comfortable reading a market trend report as you are hooking up a serial cable to debug a spanning-tree loop in the lab.
You have experience managing OEM/ODM relationships and know how to hold external engineering teams accountable to strict quality and firmware standards.
You understand that in an extensive hardware portfolio, strategy is realized through rigorous execution, BOM optimization, and reliable technical sustainment
Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, Computer Science, Telecommunications, or a related technical field; OR equivalent hands-on experience with a proven track record in hardware validation and network engineering.
Industry certifications such as CCNA, CCNP, CompTIA Network+, or equivalent industrial networking certifications are highly preferred and can substitute for formal education requirements.


EDUCATION AND CERTIFICATIONS
Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, Computer Science, Telecommunications, or a related technical field; OR equivalent hands-on experience with a proven track record in hardware validation and network engineering.
Industry certifications such as CCNA, CCNP, CompTIA Network+, or equivalent industrial networking certifications are highly preferred and can substitute for formal education requirements.

When the call goes unanswered, the opportunity is often lost.

Most SMBs cannot staff every phone line, department, location, and language around the clock. HighLevel's Voice AI product is designed to change that.

About Us

For the last three years, we have been the #1 seller of wholesale payment systems worldwide. At Volante, we are all about revolutionizing the world of Payments.

You will own the behaviour of a specific AI system or workflow inside a larger product. You will work with a team and a defined set of internal stakeholders. Your primary stakeholders are business teams who will use the workflow and engineering teams who will build it. You will be responsible for creating a spec that the business teams can approve and engineering teams can build efficiently. Your success is measured by whether the AI system behaves as specified in production over time.

You will work with QA and engineering to build and review evaluations. This is a critical part of the role. Evaluations are how you verify the AI system keeps behaving as specified once it's live.

Building a working understanding of how AI systems work, and what that means for product and analytics, is critical to this role. You will also act as a proxy for the business team and run UAT.

Alongside that, the role carries the usual weight of product ownership: picking up an unfamiliar domain fast, holding the line on scope, and keeping stakeholders aligned on what is shipping and when.

What you will own
Backlog and delivery
Own and prioritise the backlog for your system; run refinement, planning, and acceptance with the delivery team. You could also be running kanban boards for your team for a fast paced project.
Turn business requirements into AI system requirements for the engineering team.
The requirements should meet the Jeavio guardrails of AI governance, privacy, security and responsible AI standards, and highlight it when a requirement falls outside them.
Support adoption: training, workflow changes, review Evals, user manuals, release notes etc. that might be required to get the feature to production.

PO Competency
Pick up a new domain quickly and get to the point where you can ask informed questions about the business.
Should be able to adopt AI tools like Claude or similar to work upon eliciting and/or prototyping requirements (including UX designs) independently or collaboratively with technical peers.
Should be able to participate in and lead (where appropriate) discovery sessions to be able to understand the lay of the land, vision and translate it back into documentation that can be used by both the business and engineering teams.
You should be able to figure out which are the relevant metrics for users and business.
AI can be more accurate but slower, more flexible but less predictable, cheaper but occasionally wrong. You should be able to weigh tradeoffs from a product point of view - i.e. whether a certain trade off is okay or breaks user experience.
The Evals you define must align with the product requirements.

Stakeholder Management
Steer stakeholders towards the better option or push back on scope during scope based negotiations by working alongside the engineering team.
Be able to influence the roadmap by understanding what the team can deliver vs what the stakeholders want.
Should also be able to present project status to stakeholders and give an update on delivery timelines by aligning with the technical teams.
Should be able to understand and communicate the limitations of the system, clearly to stakeholders.
Behavioural specification
Write acceptance criteria for probabilistic outputs.
Work with Engineering and QA colleagues to define system guardrails
Specify the confidence thresholds that trigger human review, a fallback path, or a graceful exit.
Read and assess system prompts well enough to tell whether they match the spec.
Write the spec for two readers at once: the AI engineer who implements it and the business user who will live with it.

Evaluation and human oversight
Own the evaluation dataset for your system across its lifecycle.
Interpret results and translate them for non technical stakeholders.

Security & Compliance:
Define and prioritize security requirements in product backlog
Ensure data protection, privacy, and compliance with ISO 27001 policies
Collaborate with engineering and security teams for secure product delivery
Manage risks related to features, integrations, and data handling
Support audit readiness and continuous security improvements

What we are looking for
Required
6+ years in product ownership, product management, or business analysis, including at least two years owning a backlog with a delivery team.
Direct experience shipping or operating an AI/ML or LLM-based feature in production — not only prototyping.
Fluency in AI tools - ChatGPT or Claude including an understanding of skills, plugins, and context management.
Demonstrable understanding of how LLMs work and how they impact product decisions
Demonstrated ability to write acceptance criteria for a non-deterministic output.
Working fluency in Evals.

Role Overview:

As the Staff Product Manager for HardPhones, SIP, IVR, and Call Center, you will own the strategy, execution, and architectural evolution of HighLevel's enterprise voice and contact center infrastructure. You will lead the products and platforms that power SIP communications, physical IP phones, IVR experiences, voice routing, our multi-provider communications middleware, and native Call Center (CCaaS) features.

You will define the roadmap for building a carrier-agnostic voice platform that enables reliable, scalable, and intelligent voice communications across multiple CPaaS providers. Crucially, this scope extends into Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS). You will architect and scale our native Call Center features, developing sophisticated routing logic, agent workspaces, and queue management systems.

This role sits at the intersection of communications infrastructure, telecom engineering, voice automation, contact center operations, and platform scale. You will partner closely with Engineering, Operations, Product, Support, and external communication providers to build the next generation of HighLevel's voice platform.

Key Responsibilities:

Own the vision, strategy and execution for HighLevel's HardPhone, SIP, IVR, Call Center and Enterprise Voice platforms.
Build a scalable, provider-agnostic communications platform that abstracts multiple CPaaS providers through a unified architecture.
Architect and scale sophisticated Automatic Call Distributor (ACD) capabilities, including skills-based routing, priority queues, ring groups, overflow rules, business hours and failover logic.
Design intuitive softphone experiences across web and mobile, along with real-time supervisor dashboards for monitoring, coaching and workforce management.
Own the complete lifecycle of HardPhone provisioning, including Zero-Touch Provisioning (ZTP), remote configuration, firmware management, inventory management and device lifecycle operations.
Drive the evolution of IVR and Voice AI, including drag-and-drop workflow builders, conversational AI, speech recognition, call transcription, agent assistance, and call summarization.
Build enterprise telephony capabilities including call recording, voicemail, conferencing, whisper/barge, monitoring, queue management and compliance recording.
Define extensible Voice APIs, SDKs, webhooks and event frameworks that enable seamless integrations with third-party applications and ecosystem partners.
Lead customer migration initiatives, including provider migrations, number portability, hosted phone onboarding, and enterprise telephony transitions, while minimizing customer disruption.
Partner with Engineering, Infrastructure, Security, Compliance, Support and Go-to-Market teams to deliver highly reliable, globally scalable voice products.
Establish and monitor platform KPIs including call completion rates, SIP reliability, provisioning success, IVR containment, routing efficiency, call quality (MOS), queue abandonment, agent utilization, billing accuracy, platform availability and customer satisfaction (CSAT).
Develop and execute the long-term roadmap for enterprise telephony, AI-powered communications, multi-vendor architecture and next-generation voice experiences, ensuring HighLevel maintains competitive parity and platform leadership.

Requirement:

8+ years of Product Management experience, including ownership of communications, telecommunications, voice infrastructure, CPaaS, CCaaS or enterprise platform products.
Deep understanding of SIP, RTP, WebRTC, VoIP, IVR, enterprise telephony, and contact center ecosystems.
Proven experience building communications infrastructure or voice platform products at scale, including Automatic Call Distributor (ACD), intelligent routing and Call Center functionality.
Strong understanding of SIP endpoint management, HardPhone provisioning, remote device management, and telephony lifecycle management.
Experience working directly with CPaaS providers, telecom operators, hardware vendors, or communications infrastructure platforms.
Experience building multi-provider routing, abstraction layers, middleware, or API-first platform products.
Experience designing scalable multi-tenant platforms and highly available distributed systems serving enterprise customers.
Strong understanding of intelligent routing, least-cost routing (LCR), provider redundancy, failover mechanisms, and global telephony architecture.
Strong analytical and data-driven decision-making skills, with experience defining platform KPIs and using analytics to drive product strategy.
Demonstrated ability to define long-term platform strategy, influence executive stakeholders, and lead cross-functional initiatives across Engineering, Infrastructure, Finance, Operations, and Go-to-Market teams.
Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and prioritization skills, with the ability to simplify complex technical concepts for diverse audiences.

Nice-to-Have:

Familiarity with SIP infrastructure technologies.
Experience building conversational AI, speech recognition, voice automation, AI-powered call routing or agent assist capabilities.
Familiarity with STIR/SHAKEN, CNAM, E911, number portability, hosted numbers (BYOC/BYON), and regulatory compliance across global telephony markets.
Experience building contact center (CCaaS) capabilities such as workforce management, quality monitoring, call recording, coaching, and supervisor tools.
Experience working with event-driven architectures, APIs, SDKs, and developer platforms for communications products.
Understanding of enterprise security, privacy, and compliance requirements for voice platforms, including GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, or similar standards.

Core KPIs:

Voice Platform Reliability – SIP session success rate, call completion rate, provider failover success.
Call Center Efficiency – Queue Abandonment Rate, Average Handle Time (AHT), Agent Utilization.
HardPhone Provisioning – Device onboarding success rate, provisioning time, firmware deployment success.
IVR Performance – IVR containment rate, workflow completion, conversational AI adoption.
Routing Efficiency – Least-cost routing optimization, latency reduction, provider utilization.

Why Join HighLevel?

At HighLevel, we foster an exciting and dynamic work environment driven by a passionate team.

As we establish our India Engineering Center of Excellence (COE), we are looking for an experienced Senior Product Owner to lead delivery of Privileged Access Management (PAM), our capabilities for securing, brokering, and auditing access to privileged credentials.

This role will own the product backlog and day-to-day execution across privileged account discovery, credential vaulting and check-out, just-in-time (JIT) access requests, approval workflows, session brokering and recording, policy enforcement, and audit/compliance reporting spanning the admin console, vault, and integrations with target systems. You will work closely with Product Management, Engineering, Design, Security, Customer Success, Sales, and selected enterprise customers to turn complex privileged-access requirements into intuitive, reliable, and auditable product experiences.

The ideal candidate combines strong product-delivery discipline with a working understanding of Privileged Access Management (PAM), identity and access management (IAM), least-privilege principles, and enterprise security and compliance needs.

What You Will Do

Own and manage the PAM backlog: write, refine, and prioritize user stories, acceptance criteria, and technical tasks in collaboration with engineering and product management.
Drive sprint planning and backlog grooming, ensuring stories capture privileged-session behaviors, approval-chain logic, credential rotation, and target-system integration edge cases.
Serve as the primary point of contact for the engineering team during delivery clarifying requirements for JIT access requests, time-bound credential leasing, session recording/replay, and policy enforcement.
Partner with Product Management to translate PAM strategy into well-defined epics, milestones, and sprint-ready work, including standing privilege elimination, ephemeral access, and break-glass workflows.
Manage work across multiple product surfaces admin console, vault, approval interfaces, and integration APIs tracking dependencies and maintaining alignment across teams.
Set and manage delivery timelines: maintain realistic sprint and milestone forecasts, surface risks early, and communicate timeline changes clearly to stakeholders before they become surprises.
Collaborate with Design, QA, Security, and Compliance to define acceptance criteria that support secure, reliable, and auditable customer experiences.
Ensure requirements account for governance, separation of duties, approval chains, session auditability, and privileged-access lifecycle management (provisioning through de-provisioning).
Track and communicate sprint progress, delivery risks, decisions, and dependency status to Product and Engineering leadership.
Engage with customer feedback, support escalations, and enterprise security/compliance stakeholders to refine story prioritization and surface unmet workflow needs.
Identify, coordinate, and manage cross-functional dependencies throughout the product development lifecycle
Support release planning, readiness reviews, launch coordination, and post-release evaluation
Use AI tools and automation to accelerate discovery, requirements writing, story creation, documentation, and delivery workflows.
Understand software fundamentals relevant to PAM, including APIs, integrations, data models, authentication, authorization, and privileged-session brokering.
Understand core identity and security concepts such as least privilege, role-based and attribute-based access control, policy enforcement, approvals, session recording
Understand cloud-based and self-hosted product considerations, including configuration, deployment, licensing, and version compatibility across customer environments.

Your primary mission is to drive the delivery of high-quality, compliant software by ensuring our development teams have the clarity and context needed to execute effectively, sprint after sprint. This is a role for a product owner — someone who thrives on execution, champions quality, and is passionate about building world-class technology solutions in a dynamic, global financial environment.

What You'll Do

Backlog Ownership & Agile Execution
Own and Master the Backlog: Meticulously create, refine, and prioritize the product backlog, ensuring it is transparent, well-understood, and always ready for at least two sprints ahead.
Translate Vision into Action: Deconstruct complex business requirements into well-defined Epics, User Stories, and precise Acceptance Criteria, ensuring a high percentage of stories are accepted without rework.
Drive Sprint Success: Serve as the dedicated point of contact for the engineering team, providing unwavering clarity during sprint planning, daily stand-ups, and throughout the development cycle to remove ambiguity.
Solution Definition & Quality Assurance
Define the "What": Partner with business stakeholders to elicit, analyze, and document requirements, defining the precise solution to be built.
Champion Quality: Drive a quality-first mindset with a relentless focus on clear, testable acceptance criteria to minimize ambiguity and reduce critical defects in UAT.
Demonstrate Value: Conduct compelling demos of new functionalities to stakeholders, showcasing the value delivered and gathering immediate feedback for iterative improvement.
Stakeholder Collaboration & Domain Leadership
Build Partnerships: Act as the key liaison between business users, engineering teams, UX and other technology partners, fostering a collaborative environment to ensure seamless delivery.
Become the SME: Develop a deep expertise in your assigned Controls Technology modules, becoming the recognized go-to subject matter expert for the team and key stakeholders.
Facilitate with Purpose: Lead and actively contribute to all agile ceremonies, ensuring refinement and planning sessions are efficient, productive, and outcome focused.
Innovation in Execution
Leverage AI Tools: Utilize cutting-edge AI tools to accelerate requirements analysis, improve the quality of user story documentation, and enhance feature file generation.
Mitigate Risk Proactively: Identify and flag potential risks and dependencies that could impact schedule or quality, and work with leadership to drive mitigation strategies.

What We're Looking For

Core Qualifications:

Experience: 8+ years of experience in a technology-centric role within the financial services industry, including 5+ years as a dedicated, execution-focused Product Owner in an Agile/Scrum environment.
Domain Expertise: Proven background in Risk and Controls, Operational Risk, or Regulatory functions.
Agile Product Experties: Deep, hands-on expertise in managing a product backlog, writing high-quality user stories, and leading agile ceremonies.
Technical Fluency: A strong ability to understand technical concepts and engage in detailed discussions with engineering teams on feasibility and solutioning.
Education: Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (e.g., Computer Science, Engineering, Finance). A management degree such as an MBA is a plus.

Certifications: Industry-recognized certifications such as CSPO, A-CSPO, PSPO, SAFe POPM, or CBAP are highly desirable.
Tooling: Expert-level proficiency with agile management software (e.g., Jira, Confluence).

We do this by exposing various APIs collectively called Google Maps Platform (GMP). Working closely with regional Product Management, Commercial, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Procurement, Finance, Technology, and external manufacturing partners, the Product Manager provides thought leadership and decision support for strategic initiatives that maximize value creation across the India business.

ABOUT DBMCI ONE

DBMCI One is a learning platform for medical students and doctors, a product of NHPL (Neuroglia Health Private Limited), a subsidiary of M3, Inc., Japan's largest healthcare company, listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

NHPL is also the company behind Marrow, India's largest and most trusted learning platform for NEET PG preparation.

DBMCI One brings together the legacy of Dr. Bhatia's Medical Coaching Institute, trusted by generations of medical aspirants, with the product velocity and data discipline of a modern tech company. We are building the definitive learning platform for India's next generation of doctors: one that adapts to how each aspirant learns, making the journey from preparation to practice measurably better.

The stakes are real. The ambition is bigger.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a Product Manager to own the learner growth and engagement charter at DBMCI One. This is not a coordination role. It is a high-ownership position where you define what keeps a medical student coming back every day, what drives them from trial to deep engagement, and what ultimately makes them succeed.

You are joining at an inflection point. The habits and learning outcomes you shape today will determine how thousands of medical students learn, and in turn, how they diagnose, treat, and care for millions of patients tomorrow.

You will work hand-in-hand with Engineering, Design, Content, Data, and Marketing to ship a product that moves real numbers and real lives.

AI is not a tool you will be asked to explore here. It is the default. You are expected to prototype, automate, and iterate using AI natively from day one.


WHAT YOU'LL OWN

  • Own the full growth loop: Activation Engagement Habit Formation Retention for DBMCI One learners across platforms.
  • Define and drive the product roadmap for learner-facing features, from discovery through experimentation, launch, and post-launch iteration.
  • Use AI-assisted prototyping and vibe-coding tools to independently build and test product ideas, reducing dependence on full engineering cycles for early validation.
  • Design and run GTM experiments: scope the hypothesis, build a lean version, get it in front of real users, gather feedback, and iterate fast before committing to a full build.
  • Design and run A/B experiments at pace. Test hypotheses, kill what does not work, and double down on what does.
  • Conduct structured user research: interviews, session analysis, and cohort studies to uncover the real reasons learners drop off or stay hooked.
  • Identify leading indicators of learner success and build features that move them, not vanity metrics.
  • Use agentic AI and automation workflows to accelerate research synthesis, user feedback analysis, and product iteration cycles.
  • Write crisp PRDs, define acceptance criteria, and partner with Engineering and Design through the full delivery cycle.
  • Own the metrics framework for your charter. Build dashboards, present to leadership, and stay fully accountable for outcomes.
  • Work closely with the Content and Academics teams to ensure product and pedagogy reinforce each other.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • 2 to 4 years of Product Management experience at a tech-first company. Consumer internet, EdTech, or mobile-first products are strongly preferred.
  • Strong product thinking grounded in user behaviour. You can articulate the "why behind the why" for any user action or drop-off.
  • Hands-on data fluency: SQL, funnel analysis, cohort analysis, and A/B experiment design. You live in data, not just talk about it.
  • AI fluency is non-negotiable. Proficient with AI-assisted prototyping and vibe-coding tools (Cursor, Bolt, Lovable, Replit, or similar). Practical experience with agentic AI workflows, automation, and prompt engineering applied to product work.
  • Technical fluency: You can hold a system design conversation with Engineering, understand API dependencies, and make informed build-vs-scope decisions.
  • Proven ability to run end-to-end GTM experiments: scope, build, launch, gather user feedback, and iterate with speed and structure.
  • First-principles thinker. You do not copy-paste frameworks; you reason from the user and the context up.
  • High ownership, low excuses. You move fast, learn faster, and take full responsibility for what ships and what it achieves.
  • Clear, structured communicator. You can align a cross-functional team with a well-framed problem statement and a sharp point of view.

Our focus is on establishing product lines that focus on key outcomes by addressing real customer pain points, modernizing legacy systems, and strengthening core fundamentals. As a result, our systems and platforms support a wide range of banking and payments capabilities, including:
1. Tachyon, our cloud-native banking stack built for population-scale systems
2. Cipher, our unified authentication platform for secure, high-volume banking environments
3. Digital Credit as a Service, enabling banks to launch credit lines on UPI
4. Elena, our intelligent and conversational AI platform for banking
5. Pixel, India s first digital-native credit card, launched in partnership with HDFC Bank, for whom we also revamped their PayZapp mobile app: Winner of the Celent Model Bank Award for Payments Innovation 2024
6. Sparrow, the leading card experience for non-prime cardholders in the US and more across cards, payments, lending, and core banking.
We are an engineering-first organization that values ownership, bias for action, and long-term thinking. Together, we solve some of the hardest problems in banking tech. Our culture is built around trust, collaboration, and creating the conditions for you to drive impact proportionate to your potential. Reinforcing our commitment to creating an inclusive and supportive workplace, we have been consistently recognized as a Great Place to Work.
If you want to build cutting-edge banking tech that enables banks to serve millions reliably, securely, and at a population scale, Zeta is your playground.
If you would like to learn more about how we have grown and evolved over the years, watch our journey here . You can also explore our website and follow us on LinkedIn , Instagram, YouTube , and X .
About the Product
Zeta is building a new consumer banking product for the US market. The focus is learning fast which features drive adoption, engagement and retention - and building them well.
About the Role
Youll help grow the product through a steady cadence of experiments and feature launches. Each PM owns a business-outcome metric for one area of the product, and the roadmap that moves it. Example areas: onboarding and activation, engagement and retention, revenue, and trust and risk.
We need a hustler. The work will feel like a very early-stage startup: ambiguous problems, incomplete information, shifting priorities and no playbook. Youll bring structure to the chaos: find the answers, make the calls and get things shipped.
We expect PMs to use AI tools across the lifecycle - research, specs, prototyping, analysis - to keep iteration cycles short. PMs here go deep on how things are built, so hands-on software development experience is mandatory.
Responsibilities
1. Own a metric
  • Own a business-outcome metric for your area, plus the guardrail metrics it must not trade away.
  • Keep a ranked backlog of experiments and features, prioritised by expected impact (RICE, ICE or similar).
2. Run experiments
  • Write each bet as a hypothesis with a primary metric, guardrails and a decision rule, all set before launch.
  • Match the method to the traffic: A/B tests and holdouts at scale; fake doors, usability tests and cohort analysis at low volume.
  • Size tests properly, report null and negative results as plainly as wins, and make the ship, iterate or kill call.
  • Keep a running log of what was tested, what was learned and what changed.
3. Build features
  • Take features from problem definition through spec, build, QA, launch and adoption.
  • Write specs engineers can build from: flows, edge cases, failure states, event instrumentation and acceptance criteria.
  • Work through technical design with engineering - APIs, data models, ledger and payment flows, third-party integrations - and make trade-off calls quickly.
4. Measure
  • Define output metrics (acquisition, activation, revenue, engagement) and the input metrics that drive them (funnel conversion, feature usage).
  • Own event instrumentation and data quality for your area.
  • Do your own analysis in SQL, product analytics tools (such as Mixpanel, Amplitude or MoEngage) and BI tools (such as Metabase or Superset).
5. Research users
  • Run continuous discovery with US customers through remote interviews, usability tests and surveys.
  • Turn what you hear and what the data shows into clear problem statements that feed the backlog.
6. Shape the UX
  • Partner with designers on simple flows that earn users trust.
  • Own product copy for your area.
7. Launch and support
  • Ship behind feature flags and in stages, with monitoring and a rollback plan.
  • Work with compliance, risk, banking partners, operations and support so every launch meets regulatory requirements and can be supported from day one.
Skills
  • Statistics and experiment design: hypothesis testing, significance, power and sample sizing, and common traps such as peeking and novelty effects.
  • Strong SQL, and fluency with product analytics and BI tools.
  • Ability to work through messy data sets and turn them into decisions.
  • Engineering fundamentals you still use: reading code, system design, APIs and data models.
  • A keen eye for design, and strong UX writing.
  • Clear written and verbal communication - specs and experiment readouts people can act on.
  • Meticulous program management across parallel workstreams.

FourKites is looking for a sharp, curious and execution-focused Product Manager to join the Visibility team and own our Over-the-Road (OTR) portfolio: Truckload, LTL, Parcel and Last Mile. This is FourKites flagship product line. Some of the worlds largest shippers use it to track billions of dollars of freight every day.

This is not a PM role. You will own real product outcomes from day one. Youll work hands-on with data, build your own prototypes, talk directly with enterprise customers, and partner with engineering and design to ship features that improve adoption, retention and tracking quality.

The role sits where supply chain operations meet modern software product development, and youll need both. You need deep empathy for how freight actually moves across modes, and the analytical rigor to turn that into product bets worth making.

Responsibilities

Product Ownership Outcomes

  • Own product outcomes for one or more OTR modes (Truckload, LTL, Parcel or Last Mile), including tracking quality, ETA accuracy and carrier coverage.
  • Track and analyze adoption, engagement and retention KPIs for your area.
  • Find friction points and adoption gaps using usage data, customer interviews and feedback from Customer Success and Sales.
  • Build and prioritize a backlog that measurably improves customer stickiness, and bring well-reasoned prioritization recommendations to roadmap planning.

Data AI-Assisted Product Development

  • Write your own SQL to explore feature usage, tracking performance and customer behavior, without waiting on an analyst.
  • Use AI coding tools (Claude, Cursor and similar) to build working prototypes, internal tools and quick analyses that make a requirement concrete before engineering picks it up.
  • Work hands-on in product analytics platforms like Pendo, and maintain dashboards that track adoption trends across customer segments.
  • Turn quantitative findings into clear product hypotheses and actionable backlog items.
  • Partner with Data Science and Engineering on instrumentation and event tracking.

Customer Engagement

  • Run discovery sessions and join onboarding calls, QBRs and support escalations to understand shipper and carrier workflows firsthand.
  • Work with Customer Success Managers to surface systemic product gaps and recurring pain points.
  • Represent the voice of the customer in internal planning and sprint reviews.

Cross-Functional Execution

  • Work with Engineering and Design through scoping, development and post-launch monitoring, partnering directly with squads across time zones.
  • Support Product Marketing with onboarding materials, release notes and adoption playbooks.
  • Contribute to presales conversations and market requirements gathering with Solutions teams.

Who you are

Were hiring at two levels:

  • Associate Product Manager: 2-4 years in product management or a related role. Strong BA, analyst, solutions or implementation backgrounds in logistics tech are welcome.
  • Product Manager: 5+ years, including end-to-end ownership of a product area and a track record of shipping with measurable business impact.

For both levels:

  • Practical experience in supply chain or logistics. You understand shipper pain points, carrier dynamics and how freight moves day to day.
  • Comfort working hands-on with data: strong SQL, familiarity with analytics tools, and the ability to build a data-driven story on your own.
  • Proven use of AI tools to speed up PM work beyond drafting documents, such as building prototypes, scripts and internal tools yourself. Be ready to walk us through something youve built this way.

  • Experience working with distributed engineering teams across time zones.
  • Ability to work with significant overlap with US Central Time.

  • Experience with Pendo, Amplitude or similar product analytics tools.
  • Familiarity with agile development and working directly with engineering squads.
  • Bachelors degree in engineering, operations, supply chain, economics or another quantitative field.

What success looks like in year 1

  • You independently own a product area within OTR visibility, with clear adoption and engagement KPIs.
  • Youve shipped customer-facing improvements end to end, from discovery through post-launch analysis, with significant business impact.
  • You use data to find insights before anyone has to ask for them.
  • Youve built prototypes or internal tools that changed how a requirement was scoped or how your team works.
  • Customer Success and Engineering see you as a reliable, high-signal partner.

About VikingCloud:

VikingCloud is the leading Predict-to-Prevent cybersecurity and compliance company, offering businesses a single, integrated solution to make informed, predictive, and cost-effective risk mitigation decisions faster. Job Description:

As a Senior Product Manager of Managed Security Testing at VikingCloud, you will be responsible for the strategic planning, development, and execution of our offensive security testing services, including penetration testing as a service (PTaaS), vulnerability assessments, phishing simulations, social engineering testing, and specialized security assessments. You will own the product roadmap for VikingCloud's managed security testing portfolio, working closely with our internal security testing teams, third-party testing partners, and customers to deliver high-quality offensive security services that help merchants and financial institutions identify and remediate security weaknesses before attackers can exploit them.


This role requires deep understanding of offensive security methodologies, industry certifications and frameworks (CREST, PTES, OWASP, PCI DSS ASV), and the ability to bridge technical security testing with compliance requirements. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams including security consultants, engineering, sales, and customer success to build scalable, automated testing platforms while maintaining the rigor and quality expected from professional security assessments. Your work will directly support customers' compliance programs (PCI DSS, SOC 2, ISO 27001) while providing actionable security insights that reduce risk.

This includes an “AI Red Teaming” strategy and packages for testing the robustness of customer-facing AI applications.
  • PTaaS Platform Development: Lead the development of VikingCloud's Penetration Testing as a Service (PTaaS) platform, creating modern delivery mechanisms that provide continuous testing, real-time reporting, seamless remediation tracking, and collaborative workflows between testers and customers. Define platform requirements for test scoping, scheduling, execution tracking, finding management, retesting, and certification delivery.
  • Testing Methodology & Standards: Ensure all security testing services adhere to industry-recognized methodologies and frameworks including CREST standards, Penetration Testing Execution Standard (PTES), OWASP Testing Guide, NIST SP 800-115, and PCI DSS testing requirements. Maintain current knowledge of CREST accreditation requirements and ensure VikingCloud's services meet or exceed these standards. Define quality assurance processes for testing deliverables.
  • Certification & Compliance Alignment: Build security testing services that directly support customer compliance requirements including PCI DSS (ASV scanning, segmentation testing, penetration testing), SOC 2 Type II (security testing evidence), ISO 27001, NIST frameworks, and industry-specific regulations. Position testing services as essential compliance components that provide both security value and audit evidence.
  • Roadmap Planning & Prioritization: Create and maintain detailed product roadmaps for testing services and PTaaS platform capabilities.   • Service Delivery & Scalability: Design service delivery models that enable VikingCloud to scale testing services efficiently while maintaining quality. Define when to use internal testers versus third-party partners, automation versus manual testing, and on-demand versus scheduled assessments. Create standardized testing packages for common use cases while allowing customization for complex environments.
  • Vulnerability Management Integration: Integrate security testing services with VikingCloud's existing vulnerability scanning and management capabilities. Create workflows that enable customers to move seamlessly from continuous scanning to targeted penetration testing to remediation verification. Build unified vulnerability management dashboards that combine scan results, pen test findings, and remediation status.

Conduct market research on offensive security trends, emerging attack techniques, and evolving compliance requirements. Translate customer insights into actionable product requirements and service offerings.

Define platform capabilities that make testers more efficient and effective. Create standardized reporting templates, finding libraries, and testing playbooks that improve consistency and quality across the testing team.

Define qualification criteria for external testers including required certifications (CREST, OSCP, GPEN), experience levels, and specializations. Build marketplace or partner program for managing external testing resources.

Job Title: Associate Product Manager Shift: UK  

The Team 

Morningstar’s Analytics group develops and delivers proprietary methodologies, calculations, and analytical capabilities that help investors evaluate investments and make informed decisions. The Managed Investment Calculations team translates Morningstar’s research and intellectual property into accurate, scalable, and consistent analytics used across Morningstar products.   

The Role 

We are seeking a Associate Product Manager with strong business analysis and data analysis skills to lead the development and ongoing enhancement of managed investment calculation capabilities. 

This role combines product ownership with hands-on analytical work. You will partner with methodology experts, quantitative researchers, engineering, and quality assurance teams to translate investment methodologies and business needs into detailed calculation specifications and reliable production capabilities. You will analyze complex investment datasets, prototype and validate calculations, investigate discrepancies, and ensure that implementations faithfully reflect Morningstar’s proprietary methodologies. 

The ideal candidate brings analytical rigor, relevant investment knowledge, and the ability to learn complex financial concepts quickly. You should be comfortable both prioritizing a product backlog and using SQL to investigate underlying data. Prior knowledge of Morningstar’s products or methodologies is not required.   

Responsibilities 

  • Own product priorities and delivery: Manage the tactical roadmap and backlog for managed investment calculations, balancing new capabilities, methodology enhancements, data quality, and platform improvements. 

  • Define business requirements: Partner with product teams, research, operations, and client support to clarify user needs, assess business impact, and establish scope and success criteria. 

  • Translate methodologies into calculation specifications: Work with methodology owners to document formulas, input requirements, eligibility rules, calculation frequency, exceptions, and expected outputs. 

  • Perform detailed data and business analysis: Use SQL and analytical tools to investigate datasets, assess coverage and quality, map data sources, and understand dependencies and downstream impacts. 

  • Prototype and validate calculations: Develop calculation examples and independently verify results, including edge cases, missing data, historical changes, and differences across fund structures and share classes. 

  • Drive execution with engineering and QA: Develop actionable user stories and acceptance criteria, resolve implementation questions, and partner on test scenarios, regression coverage, and release readiness. 

  • Safeguard calculation quality: Investigate discrepancies and production issues, identify root causes, and prioritize fixes based on investor, client, and business impact. 

  • Manage methodology and implementation changes: Evaluate effects on historical results and consuming products, coordinate stakeholder review, and maintain traceability between approved methodologies and production logic. 

  • Build shared understanding: Maintain clear calculation documentation and support materials that help global teams explain analytics and resolve client questions. 

  • Measure outcomes and communicate progress: Track calculation accuracy, timeliness, coverage, and adoption, while communicating priorities, dependencies, and delivery risks.   

Required Qualifications 

  • 2+ years of experience in product management, business analysis, or data analysis, preferably within investment analytics, financial data, or financial services. 

  • Strong hands-on SQL skills and experience analyzing complex datasets to validate results and investigate issues. 

  • Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous business needs and financial methodologies into precise requirements, calculation logic, and acceptance criteria. 

  • Understanding of managed investments, including mutual funds, ETFs, share classes, and concepts such as investment performance, risk, fees, and peer group comparisons. 

  • Ability to learn complex financial concepts and methodologies quickly, question assumptions, and apply that understanding to data analysis and calculation requirements. 

  • Experience specifying, prototyping, or validating analytical calculations, with close attention to data dependencies, exceptions, and reproducibility. 

  • Experience prioritizing requirements or managing a backlog and collaborating with engineering and QA teams throughout the development lifecycle. 

  • Excellent critical thinking and problem-solving skills, including the ability to distinguish data issues from methodology or implementation issues. 

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex analytical concepts to technical and business audiences. 

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate effectively across global teams. 

  • Bachelor’s degree in finance, economics, mathematics, statistics, computer science, engineering, or a related discipline.   

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Experience working with investment datasets, financial calculations, or proprietary analytical methodologies. 

  • Python or similar programming skills for data analysis, calculation prototyping, and validation.

Senior Technical Product Manager, Networking and Switches
Reports To: VP of Products
Location: Plano, TX, Lawrence, PA, or India (preferred for direct access to our hardware labs), or Remote (US).
Travel: 20%
What You Will Do
  • Technical Portfolio Strategy and Optimization: Evaluate the existing networking, converter, and console server portfolio to drive SKU rationalization, BOM optimization, and margin improvement. Identify which products to consolidate or sunset and which high-margin lines to scale.
  • OEM/ODM Vendor Architecture and Management: Act as the primary technical interface with our global manufacturing partners. Influence their roadmaps, negotiate technical SLAs, and drive root-cause analysis and supplier quality corrections for field failures.
  • Rigorous Product Engineering and QA Leadership: Own the firmware and hardware validation gate. Design and execute New Product Introduction testing, regulatory compliance verification, and automated test frameworks.
  • Level 3 Escalation Authority: Serve as the final technical escalation point for complex field failures. Perform hands-on debugging in the lab, translate field data into engineering requirements, and enforce corrective actions with vendors.
  • Engineering Impact of Compliance and Certification: Partner with the Compliance Manager, who tracks market mandates and certification requirements. You translate those mandates into hardware and firmware requirements, evaluating vendor BOMs and architectures so that component or firmware changes do not silently invalidate FIPS, TAA, UL, NERC CIP, and other relevant standards.
  • Lifecycle and Knowledge Execution: Manage the product lifecycle from NPI through End-of-Life. Build the technical documentation, training material, troubleshooting guides, firmware test checklists, and compatibility matrices that empower support, Product Ops, and adjacent product managers.
  • Cross-Portfolio Technical Collaboration: Act as the networking subject matter expert for the broader product organization, supporting Sales and Product Marketing with technical content.
Core Technical Expertise
  • Layer 2 and Layer 3 Networking Standards: VLANs (802.1Q), Spanning Tree Protocols (STP/RSTP/MSTP), link aggregation (LACP), QoS/CoS prioritization, IP routing (Static, OSPF), IGMP snooping, and security mechanisms like 802.1X and ACLs.
  • Media Conversion and Physical Layer Mechanics: Optical and copper interfaces (SFP/SFP+, RJ-45, single-mode vs. multi-mode fiber, wavelength specifications), Power over Ethernet standards, and rate-matching mechanics.
  • PoE System Engineering: PSE/PD classification and power budget validation across 802.3af, 802.3at, intelligent detection and backward-compatibility behavior, and downstream device power profiling.
  • Harsh-Environment and Industrial Specifications: Industrial hardening, wide operating temperatures, high EMC/EMI immunity, redundant power inputs, ring redundancy protocols, and DIN-rail or panel-mount deployment.
  • Out-of-Band Management and Connectivity Protocols: Console server architectures, secure out-of-band access, terminal emulation, serial-over-IP encapsulation, and USB extension technology.
  • Security, Authentication, and Compliance Implementation: How standards are physically and logically implemented in networking gear, including TPM 2.0, FIPS 140-2/3 validated cryptographic modules, TAA-compliant supply chains, and NERC CIP supporting features; AAA frameworks (TACACS+, RADIUS, Kerberos, 802.1X) and VPN technologies (OpenVPN, IPsec) as applied to secure out-of-band platforms; plus ZTP, RESTful API, and SNMP/LLDP/NTP integration.
  • Serial and Signal Extension Technologies: Classic serial interfaces (RS-232, RS-422, RS-485) and V.35/Coax signal conversion, along with the electrical principles of signal attenuation, impedance matching, and long-distance copper extension.
  • OT and Industrial Serial Practice: Modbus ASCII/RTU over RS-422/485, and serial line conditioning including bias, termination, isolation (eg, 2-kV), and surge protection.
Who Will Succeed in This Role
  • You are a hands-on technical leader who is just as comfortable reading a market trend report as you are hooking up a serial cable to debug a spanning-tree loop in the lab.
  • You have experience managing OEM/ODM relationships and know how to hold external engineering teams accountable to strict quality and firmware standards.
  • You understand that in an extensive hardware portfolio, strategy is realized through rigorous execution, BOM optimization, and reliable technical sustainment
  • Bachelor s degree in electrical engineering, Computer Science, Telecommunications, or a related technical field; OR equivalent hands-on experience with a proven track record in hardware validation and network engineering.
  • Industry certifications such as CCNA, CCNP, CompTIA Network+, or equivalent industrial networking certifications are highly preferred and can substitute for formal education requirements.
EDUCATION AND CERTIFICATIONS
  • Bachelor s degree in electrical engineering, Computer Science, Telecommunications, or a related technical field; OR equivalent hands-on experience with a proven track record in hardware validation and network engineering.
  • Industry certifications such as CCNA, CCNP, CompTIA Network+, or equivalent industrial networking certifications are highly preferred and can substitute for formal education requirements.

Required Qualifications

Own a Flights problem space end-to-end - not a screen, not a funnel stage. Youll take the traveller journey across shopping, booking, and post-booking and be accountable for how it performs commercially and how it behaves when reality intervenes: fares that move, tickets that fail, schedules that change, and travellers who need to cancel.
The scope deliberately spans surfaces. Metasearch and comparison remain central to how travellers find us, but the interesting problems now sit in the seams - where a supplier switch at booking time creates a support contact three days later, where a baggage allowance we didnt parse at search time becomes a refund dispute, where the fare rule we couldnt read at purchase becomes a $700 agency debit memo six months on.
This is an individual contributor role with real leverage. Youll lead cross-functional squads across Engineering, Design, Data Science, Supply, Commercial, Finance Ops, and Customer Support, and youll be measured on outcomes - conversion, traffic quality, provider performance, cost-to-serve, retention - not on shipping velocity.
What youll actually work on
These are live, funded programmes, not aspirations. The detail will shift the shape wont. Here are some examples of problems you ll need to solve.
Zero Touch - self-service refunds and exchanges. Most of our contact-centre volume is travellers asking whether they can cancel or change, and most of them dont proceed once they see the cost. Youll make that answer instant, accurate, and self-serve - genuinely end to end, including back-office execution and finance reconciliation. A refund that looks automated to the traveller but spawns four manual touches behind the scenes hasnt been automated, its been moved. Youll also design the hybrid cases, with a human in the loop.
A booking record that reflects reality. Youll help define a store that traces a trip across its full lifecycle with every money movement attached, and that reconciles sources when they disagree - which they do, sometimes on the same booking, in ways that cost us real money.
Untangling the money. Payment fees, markups, booking fees, supplier costs, penalties, and the residue of every reprice, currently spread across a dozen-plus spreadsheets and recurring arguments about which one is right. Youll work with Finance Ops on the mid-office layer that puts it all on one record - including the honest build-versus-buy call.
The hard part: what makes automation here different
Read this as a preview of your first quarter, not as a warning.
  • 90% accurate is not a pass. In most products a heuristic thats right nine times out of ten is a win. Here, the 10% is a traveller told their ticket was refundable when it wasnt - so we either break a promise or eat the loss - or a void we shouldnt have processed, which returns as an airline debit six months later with a penalty attached. Youll have to reason about failure cost per decision, not aggregate accuracy.
  • The truth is spread across systems that dont agree. There is no single row you can trust. Much of this work is deciding what the source of truth is before you can automate anything on top of it.
  • Money moves before the answer is known. Funds have often already gone to the supplier by the time we decide what the traveller is owed. Product decisions here land directly on finance reconciliation, and youll need to design with that in mind rather than hand it over.
  • Complexity were choosing to keep. Continuous reprice optimization is a significant profit stream. We are not turning it off to make servicing simpler. Youll be automating on top of a system that deliberately mutates bookings after sale.
  • Some rules only exist in someones head. A real part of this role is operational design: turning tacit knowledge held by a handful of people into something a system - or an AI agent - can act on.

Position Dossier

Senior Product Manager CollectIQ

Product Management Group • Hyderabad, India


About Us

Omega Healthcare Management Services® is an AI-driven healthcare solutions company that partners across the healthcare ecosystem to deliver breakthrough results by reimagining and elevating revenue operations.

With a global presence spanning four countries, our team of 30,000+ professionals collaborates with hospitals, physician groups and healthcare providers to streamline operations, improve financial performance and elevate patient care outcomes. We combine deep domain expertise, advanced technology and a customer-centric approach to deliver innovative, scalable healthcare support solutions.

About the Omega Digital Platform®

The Omega Digital Platform® is our agentic AI engine. It leverages adaptive intelligence to drive automation across the revenue cycle, complemented by deep human expertise, to optimise performance and deliver sustained financial and clinical outcomes.

The platform spans the revenue cycle end to end — patient access and eligibility at the front, documentation and coding integrity through the middle, and revenue recovery at the back — with a shared intelligence layer running beneath all three. Capability built once on the platform is available everywhere on it.

About CollectIQ

CollectIQ is the revenue recovery product of the Omega Digital Platform. It works the accounts receivable a provider has already earned but has not yet collected — denied, underpaid, unanswered and written-off claims.

Most denied revenue is recoverable, and most of it is never recovered. Not through poor execution, but because the cost of pursuing a claim frequently exceeds what it is expected to return. The binding constraint in back-end revenue cycle management is claim economics, not staff capacity. Adding people does not solve it; lowering the unit cost of a resolution does, because it makes previously unworkable inventory worth working.

CollectIQ is built on that premise. It is an orchestration product, not a workflow tool — and the distinction defines the work.

A workflow tool assumes the work is human, and exists to make a person faster at a task a person was always going to do. CollectIQ treats the human as one execution path among several — alongside autonomous agents, digital pathways, bots and voice — selected when the economics and the confidence support it. Every claim is assessed, valued, routed to the most efficient sufficient path, resolved, written back to the client system and reconciled, with outcomes feeding back to improve the next decision.

The product is delivered as AI plus human workforce: technology does the work wherever it can, and people take only what genuinely needs judgement. Because Omega performs this work at scale across a large provider base, CollectIQ learns from real resolution outcomes — an advantage very few organisations in this market are positioned to build.

Position

Position Title: Senior Product Manager – CollectIQ

Department: Product Management Group

Location: Hyderabad, India

Reports to: Associate Vice President – Product Management

Role Type: Individual contributor

You will own a product lane within CollectIQ — one or more categories of accounts receivable, taken from zero to one. You will define the problem, scope the solution, ship it with engineering, prove it at a client, and scale it. This is a builder's role, not a backlog-administration role.

  • Write requirements engineering can build from. PRDs, user stories and acceptance criteria grounded in real claim scenarios, with clear definitions of done.
  • Define and instrument success metrics before the build. Own adoption, resolution quality, unit economics and business impact for your lane — and own building the measurement where it does not yet exist.
  • Partner across functions. Work with engineering, data science, operations, implementation and client-facing teams from discovery through go-live and iteration. Run the agile cadence your team needs.
  • Manage partner and vendor capabilities. Where we integrate rather than build, define the integration contract, the data terms and the performance bar.

ABOUT US

HighLevel is an AI-powered business operating system that gives agencies, entrepreneurs and SMBs the infrastructure to build, automate and scale. Today, HighLevel supports SMBs across 150+ countries, fueling community-driven growth rooted in real customer outcomes.

To date, businesses operating on HighLevel have generated over $7 billion in ecosystem value. By centralizing conversations, automation and intelligence into one system, we help businesses move faster, reduce complexity and execute efficiently.

Behind the platform, HighLevel powers more than 4 billion API hits and 2.5 billion message events daily. With 250 terabytes of distributed data, 250+ microservices and over 1 million domain names supported, our architecture is built for performance, resilience and long-term scalability.

OUR PEOPLE

With over 2,000 team members across 10+ countries, HighLevel operates as a global, remote-first organization built for speed and ownership. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.

OUR IMPACT

Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We're proud to be a part of that.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The B2C/Creators Product team at HighLevel is focused on building and scaling a world-class learning experience for our customers and their audiences. The platform currently serves over 1.1 million monthly active users, making it one of HighLevel's most widely adopted products. This role offers a unique opportunity to operate at scale while solving B2C-style learner experience problems within a B2B2C product ecosystem.

Events is one of the newest products in HighLevel's Memberships suite, currently in beta and being built from the ground up. It gives our customers a native way to create, publish and sell events — in-person, online and hybrid — with ticketing, RSVPs, paid and free registration, and attendee management, sitting directly alongside the contacts, communities, courses, credentials and automations they already run their business on. Organizers build and run their events from the Memberships admin; attendees live the whole thing inside Client Portal, next to the courses, communities and credentials they already sign in for.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own and Shape the B2C & Events Roadmap Partner with product leadership to help shape and execute the roadmap for HighLevel's B2C platform, serving 1.1M+ monthly active learners, with a focus on engagement, completion, and retention in a B2B2C environment.

Close the Table-Stakes Gap, Then Go Past It – Know the category cold. Get the expected capabilities right — ticket tiers, promo codes, capacity and waitlists, recurring and series events, refunds, embeddable widgets, calendar sync, wallet passes — and then decide deliberately where we go further than the incumbents rather than matching them feature for feature.

Take Events from Beta to GA – Own the beta exit criteria: the quality bar, the reliability bar, the feature completeness, and the adoption and revenue signals that tell us this product is ready to be sold broadly. Drive the program that closes those gaps.

Build Ticketing, Checkout and Payments – Lead paid, free and RSVP event types, multi-tier and multi-currency ticketing, checkout conversion, discounts, taxes, refunds and payouts — with the precision and trust a revenue-bearing flow demands, and with fee and payout terms that are a reason to choose us rather than a reason to resent us.

Give Organizers Ownership of Their Audience – Build the capability that most defines us against the category: every registration flows into the organizer's own CRM, segmentable, automatable and theirs to keep. Turn attendee data ownership from a talking point into the product's most obvious advantage.

Own Event-Day Operations – Events are judged on the day they happen. Own check-in and QR scanning, offline resilience at the door, guest lists and comp tickets, on-site sales, capacity enforcement and the operational tooling organizers depend on when things go wrong in real time.

Own the Attendee Experience in Client Portal – Client Portal is where the attendee side of Events lives, and you own it: how members find what is on, register and check out, hold their tickets, receive reminders and joining links, attend in person or online, and look back at what they have been to. Deliver that journey across both web and mobile, make events feel native to the portal rather than bolted onto it, and hold a phone-first bar throughout.

Drive Distribution and Discovery – Shape how events get found and filled: SEO-ready event pages, social and calendar syndication, embeddable listings, the Gokollab Marketplace, and the promotion tooling that turns an organizer's existing audience into attendance.

Open the Platform – Treat APIs, webhooks and integrations as a first-class surface rather than a premium upsell, so agencies and developers can build events into the workflows and client solutions they already sell.

Champion UI/UX Excellence – Partner closely with design and engineering to deliver interfaces that are intuitive, accessible, mobile-friendly and fast — for both the organizer building an event and the attendee registering for one.

Talk to Organizers Constantly – Run discovery with beta organizers, sit in on their setup, watch where they stall, and turn qualitative signal into a prioritized backlog. At this stage, direct customer contact is a primary input, not a supplement.

Experiment and Optimize – Design and analyze experiments across the funnel — event page conversion, registration completion, checkout drop-off, organizer onboarding — and iterate rapidly on evidence rather than opinion.

Support Scale, Reliability and Trust – Drive the platform work a live-event product demands: registration integrity, capacity and waitlist correctness, payment reliability, fraud and listing trust, and graceful behavior under the traffic spikes that come with a popular event going on sale.

Collaborate Cross-Functionally – Work across engineering, design, data, support, marketing and customer-facing teams to launch features, drive adoption, and close the loop on organizer feedback.

Define and Own the Metrics – Establish the success metrics for a product that does not yet have them — organizer activation, time to first published event, repeat-event rate, registration and checkout conversion, attendance rate, gross ticket volume and revenue per organizer — set the OKRs against them, and use them to steer the roadmap.

Deliver Outcomes, Not Just Features – Be accountable for measurable growth in events published, organizers activated, registrations processed and ticket revenue running through the platform.

WHO YOU ARE

B2C Experience – You have built and shipped impactful features for B2C platforms or content products, creating engaging end user experiences that drive activation, completion, and retention at meaningful scale.

An End-to-End Owner – You are comfortable owning the entire life of an event across two connected surfaces: the creator experience in the Memberships admin, where an organizer builds, prices, publishes, promotes and runs their event, and the attendee experience in Client Portal, where a member discovers it, registers, attends and looks back on it. You think in terms of the whole journey and the handoffs between those surfaces, not in terms of screens.

UX-Attentive for Learning – You bring a strong UI/UX sensibility focused on learner journeys, content discovery, progress tracking, and habit formation, with a track record of delivering intuitive and high-quality learning experiences.

jobs.descriptionHtmlOrText:
Our Company

At Teradata, we believe that people thrive when empowered with better information. Teradata Autonomous Knowledge Platform activates enterprise intelligence by unifying data, knowledge and business context to achieve tangible outcomes. With Teradata, organizations can provide agents with full context for impact when it matters. Our solution lets businesses connect and scale on premises, in the cloud, or through a hybrid approach. Teradata delivers real business value with AI.

What You'll Do

In this role, you will lead product strategy and execution for Teradata's core database engine: the massively parallel query engine behind every workload on the platform. You will shape the roadmap across the optimizer, execution runtime, workload management, and Global Planner, and own how the engine performs on native storage, cloud object storage, and open table formats such as Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake.

This role sits at the intersection of the database engine and AI. AI agents are becoming the dominant consumers of enterprise data, issuing high volumes of exploratory, speculative queries, while GenAI and machine learning can improve the engine from the inside. Every core component needs to be rethought in this light, and you will lead that rethink and turn it into a roadmap engineering can build.

Two things anchor the role. Performance: you will spend significant time inside real workloads, query plans, and benchmarks, working with engineering to deliver measurable gains release after release. SQL: you will be the steward of Teradata SQL, the surface customers live in, making its syntax, semantics, and ergonomics simpler, more expressive, and safer for developers, analysts, and AI agents.

Strategy: Own the engine vision and multi-year roadmap, co-owning architecture direction with senior engineering leaders and making principled trade-offs across performance, cost, and complexity.
AI and agents: Lead the rethink of every core engine component for AI agents as the new dominant workload, and apply GenAI and ML inside the engine to make it faster and more autonomous.
Optimizer, execution, and workload management: Agents send many redundant queries. Explore optimizing across queries, sharing intermediate results, and returning early or approximate answers. Apply learned cardinality and cost models and LLM-assisted rewrite, with guardrails that protect plan stability. Define how workload management absorbs bursty machine traffic through agent identity, priorities, and budgets.
Performance: Work hands-on with engineering on query plans, regressions, and bottlenecks. Own the benchmark suite and KPIs (latency, concurrency, plan stability, price-performance), including agentic workloads, and build regression gates into releases.
Open Table formats: Own the engine side of Iceberg and Delta Lake (scan planning, pruning, pushdown, write paths) so customers never trade performance for openness. Automate statistics, clustering, and compaction with AI.
SQL language and query interface: Design features that turn complex problems into simple, readable queries, reduce footguns while keeping power and backward compatibility, and stay aligned with ANSI SQL. Make the dialect something agents can safely generate and execute, and let agents steer with cost estimates, plan explanations, and hints.

Who You'll Work With

You will work with senior database engineering leaders, performance engineering, AI platform teams, the open table format product team, sales engineering, and executive leadership across the US, Europe, and India. This role starts as an individual contributor, leading through technical depth and influence and mentoring Staff-level PMs. It may grow into managing a team of product managers.

What Makes You a Qualified Candidate

15+ years in databases, query engines, or distributed data systems, including senior product management or equivalent principal or staff engineering experience
Expert understanding of database internals: query planning, cost-based optimization, execution models, and MPP trade-offs
Deep SQL expertise: a heavy SQL user (data engineer, analyst, or DBA) with strong opinions on language design, ergonomics, and compatibility
A hands-on performance mindset: reading query plans, designing benchmarks, and finding root causes with senior engineers
A strong working understanding of LLMs and AI agents, and an informed view on how they change database design and how ML can improve database internals
Architecture-level knowledge of Snowflake, Databricks, and ClickHouse, and fluency in lakehouse architecture and open table formats
Degree in Computer Science or a related field; an MS or PhD in databases, distributed systems, or ML for systems is a plus

What You'll Bring

First-principles thinking and good taste: willingness to question long-standing database assumptions, a preference for elegance over verbosity, customer obsession, daily use of GenAI tools, and the credibility to earn the trust of senior engineers
The ability to read research critically, separate promise from hype, and design experiments to prove value, with a track record of setting multi-year platform strategy
A plus: experience designing SQL features or language extensions, hands-on work with optimizers or learned database components, open-source contributions, or publications at SIGMOD, VLDB, or CIDR

Why We Think You'll Love Teradata

We prioritize a people-first culture because we know our people are at the very heart of our success. We embrace a flexible work model because we trust our people to make decisions about how, when, and where they work. We focus on well-being because we care about our people and their ability to thrive both personally and professionally. We are an anti-racist company because our dedication to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion is more than a statement. It is a deep commitment to doing the work to foster an equitable environment that celebrates people for all of who they are.
